question: Can accuracy above 0.80 authorize a release today?

args.reason: Find release criteria based on model accuracy threshold

steps.reasoning: Find release criteria based on model accuracy threshold

result.text:
# Legacy release memo — superseded
This document is historical. The old 2024 process promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80. It is superseded by release-policy: current releases use F1 and ROC-AUC on a frozen holdout. Do not apply the old rule.

# Experiment policy — example company handbook
The golden evaluation set is held out from prompt tuning. Development queries guide revisions. Run each query three times to estimate sampling spread. Log prompt version, retrieval top_k, temperature, tokens, latency, and the full raw tool trajectory. Calibration labels are manually reviewed rather than generated by the assistant.

# Drift runbook — example company handbook
Drift monitoring compares a 70% reference sample with a 30% current sample. Significant drift means absolute mean MonthlyCharges shift exceeds 15 USD or absolute churn-rate shift exceeds 0.05. Drift triggers challenger training and evaluation, not immediate promotion. A control batch is evaluated before trusting alerts.

# Legacy release memo — superseded
This document is historical. The old 2024 process promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80. It is superseded by release-policy: current releases use F1 and ROC-AUC on a frozen holdout. Do not apply the old rule.

# Release policy — example company handbook
Production model changes require an evaluation on a frozen holdout. Promote only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. A drift alert alone never authorizes promotion. Keep the previous production version for rollback. The release approver is the project owner.

# GPU serving — example deployment choices
The planned primary model is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct served by vLLM using BF16 on a 24 GB GPU. For a 12 GB slot use an AWQ quantized model. For a cost comparison use Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. Benchmark actual latency and quality before changing production. ONNX conversion is outside this project because vLLM owns the autoregressive decoding and KV cache.

answer.answer: No. The current release policy does not allow a model to be promoted based solely on accuracy exceeding 0.80. The legacy rule that used an accuracy > 0.80 is explicitly superseded. Today a release requires evaluation on a frozen holdout and promotion only when the model’s F1 score improves by at least 0.005 and its ROC‑AUC does not drop by more than 0.01. Therefore an accuracy above 0.80 alone does not authorize a release today.
